title: Early-warning Signal Probe Plan (working)
body:
Purpose:
This note defines an "early-warning" probing layer to sit in front of canaries/A-B slices for LLM rollout experiments. Goal: detect behavioral regressions (quality, safety, cost, latency) faster than end-user signals, with low false-positive rate and clear escalation playbook for cross-functional teams.

Scope and non-goals:
- Scope: design of probe types, instrumentation checklist, experiment sizing and statistical approach, and an ops playbook for alerts during progressive exposure.
- Non-goal: replace full customer telemetry or exhaustive eval suites. Probes are lightweight signals intended to trigger targeted inspection.

Key ideas (short):
- Multi-channel probes: synthetic prompts (golden set), randomized production shadowing, and headroom stress probes (high-length / high-batch).
- Composite signal scoring: combine orthogonal measures (semantic quality, hallucination proxy, latency percentiles, token-usage delta, fallback rate).
- Short rolling baselines: use 24h and 7d baselines with decay weighting to avoid being blinded by slow drift.
- Confidence bands & hysteresis: require persistent signal for >N windows or cross-signal agreement to reduce chatter.

Probe types (concrete):
1) Golden prompt regression probes
   - Fixed set (~200 prompts) covering: API shapes (chat/generation/structured), safety edge-cases, long-context, prompt-chaining anchors.
   - Metrics: n-gram overlap to golden outputs, model perplexity delta, syntactic anomalies (truncated output), hallucination proxy (entity hallucination check against whitelist).
   - Frequency: run every 15m in canary slices, daily in control.

2) Semantic-quality quick-assess (cheap embedding drift)
   - Take a sampled control of real production queries (anonymized), compute embedding-distance to historical centroid per intent cluster.
   - Metric: median embedding distance shift, plus outlier rate > 95th percentile.
   - Use: early detection of semantic drift after model swap or quantization change.

3) Shadowed micro-ab tests
   - Synchronously duplicate 0.5% traffic to candidate model behind a shadow flag (no user-visible change). Measure end-to-end latency, error rate, fallback triggers, and rerank score shifts.
   - Metric: ratio of errors & top-k content divergence.

4) Cost & resource headroom probes
   - Synthetic high-length sequences to exercise KV cache, memory pressure, and batching inefficiencies. Monitor tail GPU memory, OOMs, and request-scheduling delays.

Signal definitions (examples):
- Latency_tail_increase: 95th percentile for candidate > baseline_95 * 1.3 AND increase sustained for 3 consecutive windows (15m windows).
- Cost_per_completion_delta: median tokens_per_request * model_compute_cost change > 10% vs baseline.
- Semantic_shift_score: median embedding distance increase > 0.18 (tunable) + >1% of requests flagged as outliers.
- Hallucination_proxy_rate: heuristics-based entity conflict rate increase > 0.5% absolute.
- Fallback_rate: automatic fallback to smaller model triggered > baseline + 0.2%.

Statistical and operational rules:
- Windows: use sliding windows of 15m; require 3/5 consecutive windows breaching threshold to reduce noise.
- Multiple hypothesis: apply simple Bonferroni correction across probe family per slice to avoid alert storm.
- Minimum sample size: for semantic probes require at least 500 samples in window to treat signal as actionable. For golden prompts use full set every run.
- A/B gating: for any A/B with live traffic, fail-open only if no composite signal violation across the three signal families (quality, safety, perf).

Instrumentation checklist (engineers):
- [ ] Wire golden-run runner under canary namespace; store outputs with request-id and run-id.
- [ ] Emit embedding centroids and per-request distance to telemetry (tag: ew_probe=semantic).
- [ ] Expose model internal counters: kv-cache hits/misses, quantization-path used, kernel-fallback events.
- [ ] Expose scheduler queue depth and GPU tail latency metrics (per model-version pool).
- [ ] Add provenance metadata to shadowed calls (slice, experiment-id, run-id).

Alerting and escalation (playbook):
- Level 1 (info): Single-signal blip (e.g., 1 window) -> notify experiment owner Slack channel with auto-created ticket in ROLL board. Owner: product/PM.
- Level 2 (investigate): Multi-signal agreement OR persistent (>3 windows) breach -> page oncall SRE + notify product+serving runtime. Quick triage checklist: reproduce on golden set, check recent deploys/PRs, check infra telemetry.
- Level 3 (stop exposure): Safety signal (hallucination_proxy > threshold) OR severe perf/cost (latency_95 up >30% or OOM) sustained -> automated traffic cutback (rollback to baseline or route to fallback) + incident response.

Stoplight decision table (quick):
- Green: no signals breached -> continue ramp.
- Yellow: 1 signal breached or transient -> freeze ramp; reduce cadence; investigator assigned.
- Red: multi-signal or safety/perf breach -> halt and rollback.

Simulation & validation plan (before adopting probes):
- 1) Replay window: run probes against last 90 days of traffic using existing model swaps / incidents to verify sensitivity / FP rate.
- 2) Spike injection: synthetic latency/cost/hallucination injections to measure detection latency and required window sizes.
- 3) Cross-team dry-run: run probe alerts in 'audit-only' for 2 weeks with oncall watching to tune thresholds.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Q1: Threshold values for semantic shift are workload-specific. Need per-product baselines. Action: product owners to provide 3 canonical intents per rollout. (Owner: Ravi)
- Q2: How to correlate embedding drift to user-visible quality (avoid chasing false positives)? Proposed: link to small human-eval sampling when semantic_shift_score > threshold.
- Q3: Should probes run for Dedicated vs Hosted differently (cost constraints)? Proposal: reduce golden frequency to 1h for high-cost Dedicated customers unless flagged. (Owner: Tomás)

Immediate next actions (this week):
- Claire: spin up golden prompt runner in dev cluster (ETA 3 days).
- Evelyn: draft alert-runbook with SRE (ETA 2 days).
- Ravi: collate canonical intents per product line (ETA 1 week).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally conservative (requires persistence + cross-signal agreement) to avoid noisy rollbacks. The goal is to give product + SRE a reproducible trigger for targeted inspection, not to be the single source of truth.
